title: Talking about books
subtitle: poignant, a page-turner, heavy going
summary: Read a blurb like a critic and describe any book precisely - from poignant and enigmatic to lightweight, heavy going or compulsive reading.

lesson.heading: What a blurb is
lesson.text: A **blurb** is the short text, usually printed on the back cover of a book, describing what the book is about and sometimes quoting critics. Blurbs use a small, very rich set of adjectives, and knowing them tells you at once what kind of book you are holding.

examples.text: Woman of Snow is a **poignant chronicle** of childhood in a small American town.
examples.note: poignant = moving and sad; a chronicle = a description of a sequence of events

examples.text: The third novel by this **acclaimed** writer, this is a **compelling** tale of mystery, love and betrayal.
examples.note: acclaimed = praised by the public; compelling = very interesting and engaging

lesson.heading: Blurb adjectives
rows: rather dark, mournful and gloomy (often used of people too)
often cruel or disgusting, concerned with death
so interesting or exciting that it holds your attention totally
humorous in the face of a bad situation

lesson.heading: More blurb words
lesson.text: A **page-turner** is a powerful story that keeps you interested. A moment of **insight** shows the ability to understand what something is really like. The **protagonist** is the main character, and a character is **eponymous** when they have the same name as the title of the book.

examples.text: A **page-turner** full of brilliant moments of **insight** and an unparalleled depth of feeling.
Jim Lawless, the **eponymous protagonist** of Arkrow's latest novel, is a confused young man seeking a meaning in life.
A **macabre** and **chilling** account of an unsolved murder that tears a village apart.

lesson.heading: Some other types of book
rows: a written record of what you have done each day; also an academic publication of articles, issued at regular intervals
a written record of a person's own life, typically by a politician or military figure
a book or set of books of articles in alphabetical order, covering the whole of human knowledge or part of it
a collection of, for example, poems or short stories by different authors
a technical book with instructions, for example a car manual
a book recording events and times, for example all the journeys made by a lorry or ship
lesson.note: An academic publication of articles issued periodically is a journal, never a magazine.

left.label: You can't stop
left.text: **Compulsive reading** is difficult to stop once you have started (formal); informally, it is a book you **just can't put down**. A book that is **informative** gives a lot of useful information.
examples: It's **compulsive reading** - I finished it in a night.
It's one of those books you just **can't put down**.
It's very **informative** about the history of Ireland.

right.label: You can't start
right.text: A book that is **lightweight** is not complex - slightly negative, though it makes good **bedtime reading**. One that is **heavy going** is difficult to read, and you may simply not **get into** it.
examples: His last one was **heavy going** and I just couldn't **get into** it.

lesson.heading: Books and their times
lesson.text: A book **ahead of its time** contains ideas that no one else had yet thought of or discussed when it appeared. A book that is **a product of its time** simply reflects the period it came from - which is often why its ideas now seem tame, old-fashioned or **gender-biased**. The **readership** is the number of people who read an author's work.

examples.text: Nancy Riley's 1950 novel about mental breakdown was **ahead of its time**.
Her 1955 book Exciting Careers for Women was **a product of its time**.
Nonetheless, his books always attract a wide **readership**.

lesson.text: Lightweight is mildly negative, heavy going is plainly negative - neither is a compliment, but only one of them takes effort.

exercises.prompt: Which type of book is each person talking about?

pairs.left: It's by General Rogers, who led the allied forces during the recent war.
It's so badly written I don't know how anyone could learn to use the machine from it.
If you want to read a typical selection of modern poets, it's excellent.
The latest issue contains a paper presenting a new theory of the human mind.

exercises.prompt: Match what you would find with the kind of book it comes from.

pairs.left: an article about waterfalls, with pictures
a record of a recent test of a lorry
an academic paper published three times a year

exercises.prompt: I just could not ___ the story, so I stopped reading it.
exercises.explanation: To get into a book is to become involved or engaged with it.

exercises.prompt: It's dense and very difficult to read - in fact it's ___ going.
exercises.explanation: A book that is heavy going is difficult to read.

exercises.prompt: It's not very serious, and it's easy to read - rather ___, in fact.
exercises.explanation: Lightweight means not complex; it carries a slightly negative connotation.

exercises.prompt: You find yourself wanting to read more - it's ___ reading, it's so fascinating.
exercises.explanation: Compulsive reading is difficult to stop once you have started.

exercises.prompt: Her second novel did not attract a large ___.
exercises.explanation: A readership is the number of people who read a writer's books.

exercises.prompt: The story takes place against a rather ___ background in 18th-century London.
exercises.explanation: Lugubrious means rather dark, mournful and gloomy; it is often used of people too.

exercises.prompt: It's full of ___ comedy and satire.
exercises.explanation: Wry humour is humour in the face of a bad situation.

exercises.prompt: The novel is a ___ portrayal of life in a coal-mining community during the last recession.
The novel's ___ heroine, Maria Selune, leaves home at the age of 18 and travels through Asia.
exercises.explanation: An eponymous character has the same name as the title of the book.

exercises.prompt: It's a very ___ novel; you never really know what is happening until right at the end.
House of the Dead is a ___ story of torture and death in a medieval castle.
exercises.explanation: Macabre means cruel or disgusting and concerned with death.

exercises.statement: Mena Harrap's self-help book was ahead of its time, but what was true in the 1980s doesn't necessarily apply nowadays.
exercises.explanation: It was a product of its time - a reflection of the period. Ahead of its time means it contained ideas nobody had yet discussed.

exercises.prompt: Would each word appear in a blurb for a dark thriller or for a warm family story?
Put this line from a blurb in order.
exercises.answer: A page-turner full of brilliant moments of insight
exercises.explanation: A page-turner is a powerful story that keeps you interested; insight is the ability to understand what something is really like.
